title: Ghostlight Optical System
description: JSON Schema for the `ghostlight-optical` lens file format. One format, one version: the loader accepts major 1 only, and the writer emits it unconditionally.

format.description: Format identifier. Must be the literal string `ghostlight-optical`.

metadata.description: Provenance. The loader reads `name` (display name) and the optional `focal_length_mm` hint; everything else is informational and preserved verbatim across a load/save round-trip. `title` is not a synonym for `name`; the display name is always `name`.

name.description: Display name. Read by the loader.

source.description: Where the prescription came from (patent, catalogue, measurement).

focal_length_mm.description: Optional EFL hint, read by the loader so callers that need a value before a paraxial trace lands have one.

glass_catalogue.description: Inline glass catalogue. Keys are catalogue keys referenced from `materials[i].glass`.

optical_system.description: Ordered source-to-image-plane sequence of elements. An `element` with N surfaces + N-1 materials models a piece of glass (singlet, cemented doublet/triplet, etc.); a 1-surface 0-material element is a first-class stop, mirror, or interface.

pivots.description: Post-process rig layer. Each pivot translates and/or rotates a named set of elements around a pivot point; the C++ loader composes pivot transforms onto the targeted elements' transforms before flattening surfaces. Multiple pivots on the same element compose in array order. The optical system is the bind pose; pivots are the rig.

version.description: The lens format version. `major` is gated by the loader; a newer `minor` loads with a warning and unknown fields ignored. Mirrors LENS_FORMAT_MAJOR / LENS_FORMAT_MINOR in ghostlight/src/optical_system.h.

uuid.description: UUID (any standard form). Used for stable cross-referencing such as ghost identification and pivot membership.

mode.description: Editor hint. `absolute` (default): x/y/z are world-frame. `relative_to_preceding`: z is interpreted as a delta from the preceding element's resolved absolute z (x/y are always absolute; rotation and decenter on the preceding element are ignored). The loader always flattens to absolute before tracing. First element with `relative_to_preceding` is a no-op (treated as absolute) and emits a warning.

pivot.description: Centre of rotation, in the element's own local frame, relative to the element origin (its first surface vertex). Omitted or all-zero rotates about that front vertex, which is the historical behaviour. Applies to `rotation` only — it does not move the element, and it does not enter the nominal axial bookkeeping (relative position chaining, inter-element air gaps, sensor rebase), all of which stay on the untilted layout. Distinct from the top-level `pivots[]` rig, which is a group-level post-process layer.

catalogue_ref.description: Provenance metadata only (e.g. `Schott:N-BK7`). Not a live reference.

C.description: Sellmeier C coefficients in micrometres squared.

id.description: Stable UUID. Identity is by UUID, not array position: the writer reassembles the flat surface array back into elements through these ids. A document that omits them loads (the loader synthesizes stable placeholders) but must not be authored that way.

element.description: An element groups N surfaces sharing one rigid-body transform. N surfaces + N-1 materials models a real piece of glass (singlet, cemented doublet/triplet, ...). 1 surface + 0 materials models a stop, mirror, or interface. The loader enforces `surfaces.length == materials.length + 1`.

glass.description: Key into `glass_catalogue`. The literal strings `air` / `AIR` are reserved and treated as vacuum / air (n = 1).

id.description: Stable UUID. Identity is by UUID, not array position: the writer reassembles the flat surface array back into elements through these ids. A document that omits them loads (the loader synthesizes stable placeholders) but must not be authored that way.

is_active.description: False mutes the surface: it is skipped by the tracer and excluded from ghost pairs. Omitted when true. This field was read and written for a long time while being absent from the schema, which -- with `additionalProperties: false` -- made every muted-surface file schema-invalid.

thickness.description: Axial distance to the next surface within the same element, in mm. Omitted on the last surface of an element.

modifiers.description: Modifier stack. At most one coating modifier is honoured per surface (last one wins); a surface is either a reflectance coating or an attenuator, not both.

radius.description: Signed radius of curvature in mm. 0 means a flat / plane surface. Positive radius = centre of curvature behind the surface.

conic_constant.description: Conic constant K. K = 0 + empty terms = sphere; K = -1 + empty terms = paraboloid.

terms.description: Polynomial sag terms starting at A4 (r^4). A2 is implicit in radius + conic_constant per ISO 10110.

ar_layers.description: AR coating layer count. 0 = uncoated, 1 = single-layer MgF2, 2+ = multi-coat approximation. Omitted is equivalent to 0.

modifier_coating_artist.description: Artist-driven coating: an RGB tint plus reflection strength, synthesized at trace time into a smooth spectral reflectance (Gaussian basis at 650/550/450 nm, partition-of-unity normalized). White tint = flat R(lambda) = strength. Angle-independent by design; stored as intent so it stays editable.

tint.description: Ghost tint as [r, g, b] in [0,1].

strength.description: Peak reflectance. 0.04 is roughly bare glass; AR coats are 0.005-0.02.

modifier_coating_spectral.description: Empirical wavelength-dependent reflectance table (e.g. manufacturer spectral data). Linear interpolation between samples.

out_of_range.description: Behaviour outside the table range: `clamp` uses the nearest edge value; `discard` kills the ray's contribution (strict / scientific use).

modifier_coating_angular.description: Incidence-angle-dependent reflectance table. Angles are measured in the reference medium given by `angle_ref_ior` (default air); lookups from inside glass convert via the Snell invariant n*sin(theta).

angle_ref_ior.description: IOR of the medium the angle axis is measured in (1.0 = air, the manufacturer-data convention).

modifier_coating_spectral_angular.description: 2-D reflectance table over wavelength x incidence angle (bilinear interpolation). `r` rows correspond to wavelengths, columns to angles. The most complete empirical coating representation.

angle_ref_ior.description: IOR of the medium the angle axis is measured in (1.0 = air).

modifier_coating_layers.description: Physical thin-film layer stack, evaluated at load time via the Transfer Matrix Method and baked to a wavelength x angle reflectance table (the tracer never runs TMM). Layers are ordered from the outer medium inward; the substrate is the lens glass. The file stays self-contained: each layer embeds its own n,k table inline. This tier used to be discriminated by the mere presence of `layers` with no `model` key -- the one coating you could not identify without inspecting the payload.

material.description: Display name (e.g. `MgF2`). Provenance only; the physics comes from nk_table.

modifier_coating_attenuator_gaussian.description: Positional amplitude attenuator: a Gaussian transmission profile over the surface (apodization / pupil shaping). Applies alongside bare-Fresnel reflectance; a surface is either an attenuator or a reflectance coating.

modifier_aperture_circular.description: Circular aperture stop. The bounding radius is the surface's `semi_aperture`; with `aperture_aspect` != 1 the bound becomes an ellipse (X half-axis = semi_aperture * aperture_aspect, Y half-axis = semi_aperture).

modifier_aperture_polygon.description: Bladed aperture stop inscribed in the bounding ellipse. With no blade-shape fields it is the regular n-gon: the vertex circle has radius `semi_aperture` (i.e. angle 0° points at a vertex by default), `rotation_deg` rotates it, and `aperture_aspect` stretches the bounding ellipse along X. `curvature`, `twist`, `notch_deg` and `notch_angle_deg` deform the blade edge; all are optional and all default to 0, which reproduces the plain n-gon exactly. Blade tips stay on the vertex circle, so deforming changes how much area the stop encloses, never its bounding radius.

curvature.description: Blade-edge waist depth. 0 = straight chord (the plain n-gon), +1 = the circumscribed circle, negative scoops the edge inward and leaves the tips as spikes.

twist.description: Where the waist sits along the blade edge. 0 = centred (symmetric blades); the extremes drive it toward a tip, which is what makes the blade handed. +t and -t are mirror images.

notch_deg.description: Tip facet depth, and by its sign which side the facet leans toward. NOMINAL degrees: the value is applied as a fraction of the blade's own sector, not as a literal angle, so the same setting gives a proportionally similar tooth at every blade count.

notch_angle_deg.description: Skew of the tip facet: 0 cuts the corner symmetrically, 45 pushes the cut fully to one side. Nominal in the same sense as notch_deg, and inert while notch_deg is 0.

modifier_aperture_image.description: Bitmap-driven aperture stop. The parser records `image_path` and `semi_diameter` on the surface; pixel data is loaded by a caller-supplied helper (typically `OpticalSystem.load_aperture_images()` on the Python side). The image is sampled in [0,1] UV space mapped to a square of half-width `semi_diameter` mm in world space.

image_path.description: Path to the bitmap (PNG, single-channel float or 8-bit greyscale). Relative paths are resolved against the lens file's directory.

semi_diameter.description: World-space radius (mm) at the image boundary. Becomes the surface's aperture_semi_diameter.

pivot.description: Post-process rig entry. Translates and/or rotates a set of elements around a pivot point. Both translation and rotation are in scope. The loader composes pivot transforms onto each targeted element before flattening surfaces; multiple pivots on the same element compose in array order. `exposed` flags which offset attributes are artist-facing controls (UI sliders); coupled/curve controls are not modelled.

elements.description: Element IDs (UUIDs) this pivot acts on.

mode.description: `centroid`: pivot point is the arithmetic mean of the targeted elements' (resolved absolute) origin positions. `manual`: pivot point is taken verbatim from x/y/z.

attr.description: Dotted path into the pivot's `offset` block that this control writes to.
